title: Dense linear orders: rational embeddings and the real line
summary: Countable orders embed in the rationals, while density and completeness characterize the rational and real orders.
abstract: Between any two rational numbers there is another, so their usual order is dense; it also has no first or last point. Among nonempty countable linear orders, these properties determine the entire order: every such order can be matched with the rationals by a bijection preserving comparison. Even a countable order without these properties can be embedded in the rational line. For nonempty dense linear orders without endpoints, the real line is characterized by two further properties: a countable subset meeting every interval, and completeness, meaning that every nonempty set bounded above has a least upper bound.

based_on.title: An Introduction to Set Theory
based_on.pages: 79–82 (Chapter 8, Theorem 29 and the complete separable order characterization)
